summary_hint: ACORD 25 Certificate of Liability Insurance #<certificate_number> for <insured_name> (holder <certificate_holder_name>); <coverage_lines> liability coverage sections. A CERTIFICATE, not a policy.

typed_core.name: certificate_date
typed_core.why: identity/processor — the certificate issue date (recency of the evidence)

typed_core.name: producer_name
typed_core.why: identity — the insurance producer/agency that issued the certificate

typed_core.name: insured_name
typed_core.why: identity — the named insured the policies were issued to (e.g. the builder / HOA / association)

typed_core.name: certificate_holder_name
typed_core.why: identity — who the certificate is furnished to (often the lender, ISAOA/ATIMA)

typed_core.name: description_of_operations
typed_core.why: processor — the free-text 'DESCRIPTION OF OPERATIONS / LOCATIONS / VEHICLES' (project, units, buyer, etc.)

typed_core.name: project_or_property_reference
typed_core.why: processor — the project/property the coverage relates to (from the operations block or the ACORD 101 remarks: project name, property address, unit)
typed_core.prompt_hint: The project/property reference (e.g. 'Senata at Research Park', a unit address); capture as printed

nested_lists.name: coverage_lines
nested_lists.shape_reason: the ACORD 25 lists several COVERAGE SECTIONS (CGL, Auto, Umbrella/Excess, Workers Comp), each with an insurer, policy number, effective/expiration dates, and limits. ONE ROW PER SECTION (the LP-460 lesson: NOT one row per sub-limit). A CGL section prints ~6 sub-limits; the row carries the section's PRIMARY headline limit, the rest fall to the catch-all. Mirrors the master_insurance coverage_lines (one limit per section).

fields.name: coverage_type
fields.why: the coverage section label: Commercial General Liability / Automobile Liability / Umbrella (Excess) Liability / Workers Compensation / Property / Crime / Fidelity — as printed

fields.name: insurer_name
fields.why: the insurer affording this coverage (Insurer A/B/... resolved to its name)

fields.name: insurer_naic_number
fields.why: the insurer's NAIC # for this coverage

fields.name: policy_number
fields.why: the policy number for this coverage section

fields.name: limit_description
fields.why: the label of the section's PRIMARY headline limit (e.g. 'Each Occurrence', 'Combined Single Limit', 'E.L. Each Accident')

fields.name: limit_amount
fields.why: the amount of that primary headline limit

rejected.name: per-sub-limit rows
rejected.reason: the LP-460 lesson applied directly — a blunt 'emit every labeled limit' fragments one CGL section into ~6 rows. The unit of capture is ONE ROW PER COVERAGE SECTION; secondary sub-limits (Damage to Rented Premises, Med Exp, General Aggregate, Products-Comp/Op) fall to the catch-all.

rejected.name: is_adequate / meets_requirement / coverage_sufficient
rejected.reason: JUDGMENTS, not facts — whether coverage satisfies a program requirement is a rule/processor call, not a value on the certificate. Tags describe; rules judge.

rejected.name: master_property_coverage / fidelity_bond_amount
rejected.reason: an ACORD 25 is a LIABILITY certificate (CGL/Auto/WC/Umbrella); it does NOT carry master-property (dwelling replacement cost) or fidelity/crime coverage. That is an ACORD 27/28 (Evidence of Property Insurance) + a crime cert — a different form. Do not invent property/fidelity fields the ACORD 25 does not print.

encoding_variations: ACORD 25 is a fixed-layout form; the coverage grid rows are CGL, Auto, Umbrella/Excess, Workers Comp (blank rows have no policy → no coverage_lines row)
an insurer is referenced as 'INSURER A/B/...' in the grid and named in the 'INSURER(S) AFFORDING COVERAGE' block with a NAIC # — resolve the letter to the name
a CGL section prints ~6 sub-limits; capture the PRIMARY (Each Occurrence) as the row limit
an ACORD 101 Additional Remarks Schedule (page 2) may carry the property address and loan number — feed project_or_property_reference (and note the loan number is scrubbed at the snapshot boundary)

open_questions.q: Certificate vs the existing master_insurance_policy_for_condominium — redundant?
options: let the master-policy type absorb it
open_questions.recommendation: SEPARATE (GEET'S DECISION, LP-467): a summary CERTIFICATE (ACORD 25 liability) is structurally and content-wise disjoint from the governing condo master POLICY; forcing 073 into the master schema (dwelling/deductible/causes-of-loss) produces garbage. Not redundant.

notes: ⚠️ CO-3 CORRECTION (LP-467): the plan tied this type to CO-3 (condo master policy + fidelity bond). THAT IS WRONG. CO-3's inputs are master-PROPERTY coverage + a fidelity/crime bond, which arrive on an ACORD 27/28 (Evidence of Property Insurance) + a crime certificate — NOT this ACORD 25 (liability). Anyone building CO-3 must NOT look for its inputs here. This type serves NO rule (rules_served empty); it earns its catalog entry on PROCESSOR VISIBILITY (a real, distinct standard document that otherwise dilutes `unknown`), the same standard as wire_instructions (ADR-362/363).
The sample 073 is a homebuilder's (Taylor Morrison) liability certificate — CGL + Auto + Workers Comp for a project — not a condo master-property/fidelity cert.

No _PII_FIELDS entry: certificate_number ('W'-prefixed), policy numbers (separator'd), NAIC (5-digit), and limits (<9 digits) do not trip the contiguous-digit guard. description_of_operations + project_or_property_reference get the 9+-digit scrub backstop (the ACORD 101 prints a bare loan number).
